entry.title: Royal Women Celebrating Diwali
entry.blurb: The style of this work is typical of Mughal painting from the mid-1700s, when scenes of domestic life among women of the court were a favorite subject for the imperial artists.

source.credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art. Andrew R. and Martha Holden Jennings Fund

facts: Lined along the eaves, the top of the marble lattice railing, and the rims of the boats on the river are candles and butter lamps lit in celebration of a New Year festival.
A princess on a golden armchair lights sparklers with her friends.
"Diwali" comes from the Sanskrit words dīpa (lamp) and āvali (rows or series).

candidate.title: Royal Women Celebrating Diwali
candidate.medium: gum tempera and gold on paper
candidate.credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art. Andrew R. and Martha Holden Jennings Fund
candidate.description: Lined along the eaves, the top of the marble lattice railing, and the rims of the boats on the river are candles and butter lamps lit in celebration of a New Year festival. A princess on a golden armchair lights sparklers with her friends. In the boats and on the far shore men set off sparklers under the light of a magnificent firework display under the full moon. The style of this work is typical of Mughal painting from the mid-1700s, when scenes of domestic life among women of the court were a favorite subject for the imperial artists. "Diwali" comes from the Sanskrit words dīpa (lamp) and āvali (rows or series).
